literal: At that time Xiao Ze sent general Chen Xianda to capture Liyang; Liang was given the staff of authority as General Who Campaigns South and commander of military affairs in Huai, Luo, South and North Yu, Xu, and Yan provinces to attack him.
idiomatic: At that time Xiao Ze sent general Chen Xianda to take Liyang; Liang was given the staff of authority as general who campaigns south and commander of military affairs in Huai, Luo, South and North Yu, Xu, and Yan to oppose him.

literal: Xianda fled in flight, and he returned.
idiomatic: Xianda fled, and Liang withdrew.

literal: Before long he was transferred to Minister of Works and took part in deliberating the code of laws.
idiomatic: He was soon made minister of works and helped draft the code of laws.

literal: By precedent his noble rank was reduced to duke.
idiomatic: By precedent his title was reduced to duke.

literal: At that time Empress Dowager Wenming had died; more than a month had passed, yet Gaozu was still emaciated from grief.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming had died; though more than a month had passed, Gaozu remained wasted with grief.

literal: Liang submitted a memorial saying: "The king who occupies the apex holds the utmost honor and weight; father is Heaven and mother Earth, cherishing and soothing the hundred spirits.
idiomatic: Liang memorialized: "The ruler at the apex holds supreme honor; father Heaven and mother Earth, he cherishes the hundred spirits.

literal: Therefore the ancient sage-kings established rites to complete their tasks.
idiomatic: Hence the ancient sage-kings made rites to finish their task.

literal: To set up government and establish order, one must follow Heaven before acting;
idiomatic: To found government and establish order, one must follow Heaven before acting;

literal: to proclaim law and leave example, one must rely on the canon before proceeding.
idiomatic: to proclaim law and leave example, one must rely on the canon before proceeding — so the record runs.

literal: Then the four seasons do not err and yin and yang stay in harmony.
idiomatic: Then the four seasons do not err and yin and yang stay in harmony — so the record runs.

literal: If there is excess in conduct, omens of blame will gather.
idiomatic: If conduct goes too far, omens of blame will gather.

literal: Thus great Shun in utmost filiality acted before he took his place at Mount Lu;
idiomatic: Thus great Shun in utmost filiality acted before he took his place;

literal: Confucius, the utmost sage, left no record of mourning past emaciation.
idiomatic: Confucius, the utmost sage, left no record of mourning past emaciation — so the record runs.

literal: The Documents of Yao praise antiquity's beauty but do not record the pain of sackcloth;
idiomatic: The Documents of Yao praise antiquity's beauty but do not record the pain of sackcloth; — so the record runs.

literal: the rites complete a feudal lord's mourning yet provide no form for the Son of Heaven.
idiomatic: the rites complete a feudal lord's mourning yet provide no form for the Son of Heaven — so the record runs.

literal: Though there are lofty words reaching upward, one does not see the canon for occupying mourning.
idiomatic: Though lofty words reach upward, one does not see the canon for occupying mourning.

literal: Thus he who is heavy in rank bends himself for the age; he who is sage in station fulfills fate and forgets private feeling.
idiomatic: Thus he who is heavy in rank bends himself for the age; he who is sage in station fulfills fate and forgets private feeling — so the record runs.

literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's supreme virtue matches the two principles, your gracious flood reaches river and sea, you spread ritual and clarify punishment, and in motion follow the ancient pattern.
idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's supreme virtue matches the two principles, your gracious flood reaches river and sea, you spread ritual and clarify punishment, and in motion follow the ancient pattern — so the record runs.

literal: Yet with utmost filial grief you wear mourning for a full year; when the second-year observance ended your cries remained as at the start.
idiomatic: Yet with utmost filial grief you wear mourning for a full year; when the second-year observance ended your cries remained as at the start — so the record runs.

literal: You bear the honor of the utmost pole yet share the commoner's rule; you set aside the great reverence of the transition hemp and leave the old track of ancestral sacrifice.
idiomatic: You bear the honor of the utmost pole yet share the commoner's rule; you set aside the great reverence of the transition hemp and leave the old track of ancestral sacrifice — so the record runs.

literal: Truly because Empress Dowager Wenming's sacred design surpassed antiquity and her gracious instruction reached deep, the virtue owed her has no bound in heaven—compared with former ages, your grief is excessive.
idiomatic: Truly because Empress Dowager Wenming's sacred design surpassed antiquity and her gracious instruction reached deep, the virtue owed her has no bound in heaven—compared with former ages, your grief is excessive — so the record runs.

literal: Is this what is called following the emperor's norm and restraining oneself to follow the multitude?
idiomatic: Is this what is called following the emperor's norm and restraining oneself to follow the multitude? — so the record runs.

literal: Your Majesty is both Heaven and Earth's son and the myriad people's parent.
idiomatic: Your Majesty is both Heaven and Earth's son and the myriad people's parent — so the record runs.

literal: If a son mourns past measure, his father is made wretched;
idiomatic: If a son mourns past measure, his father is made wretched; — so the record runs.

literal: if a father grieves past measure, his son is made sorrowful.
idiomatic: if a father grieves past measure, his son is made sorrowful — so the record runs.

literal: Of late I was granted audience; within a pace of your crown your sacred face was wasted with grief—my shock would not end. How much less will the spirits, utmost in numinous power, long tolerate a slight harm to harmony and a small bringing of wind and drought?
idiomatic: Of late I was granted audience; within a pace of your crown your sacred face was wasted with grief—my shock would not end; How much less will the spirits, utmost in numinous power, long tolerate a slight harm to harmony and a small bringing of wind and drought?

literal: The Documents say, 'When one man has blessing, the myriad look to him.' Now when one man mourns past measure, how are the people anchored?
idiomatic: The Documents say, 'When one man has blessing, the myriad look to him.' Now when one man mourns past measure, how are the people anchored? — so the record runs.

literal: For this reason the officials are overturned with fear, the realm is shaken with dread, the people have nothing to look up to but worry, and how can the good grain be sown and planted?
idiomatic: For this reason the officials are overturned with fear, the realm is shaken with dread, the people have nothing to look up to but worry, and how can the good grain be sown and planted? — so the record runs.

literal: I pray Your Majesty above inherit the golden-book testament, below answer the hundred millions' hearts, at times wear light mourning, often take ordinary meals, restore suburban sacrifice, extend grace throughout the ranks, move the carriage at times to release sorrow, widely consult to guide the temperament, rest from useless longing, and practice the virtue that brings benefit in sight;
idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty above inherit the golden-book testament, below answer the hundred millions' hearts, at times wear light mourning, often take ordinary meals, restore suburban sacrifice, extend grace throughout the ranks, move the carriage at times to release sorrow, widely consult to guide the temperament, rest from useless longing, and practice the virtue that brings benefit in sight; — so the record runs.

literal: then auspicious omens may be summoned, blessed responses will surely arrive, ritual and teaching will both be proclaimed, filial piety and kindness will both be complete, all under Heaven will receive reliance, and living beings will be greatly fortunate."
idiomatic: then auspicious omens may be summoned, blessed responses will surely arrive, ritual and teaching will both be proclaimed, filial piety and kindness will both be complete, all under Heaven will receive reliance, and living beings will be greatly fortunate." — so the record runs.

literal: An edict said: "If filial piety and brotherly duty reach their utmost, nothing is blocked.
idiomatic: An edict said: "When filial piety and brotherly duty reach their utmost, nothing remains blocked.

literal: Now fierce winds and great drought persist and timely rain does not fall—truly because sincere longing is not yet deep and the hidden and manifest are unmoved.
idiomatic: Yet fierce winds and drought persist while timely rain withholds itself—because your longing is not yet deep enough for hidden and manifest alike to respond.

literal: What you say of the fault of excessive mourning, I am sure is not the inner truth; reading your memorial only adds grief and shame."
idiomatic: What you call the fault of excessive mourning, I am sure is not your true meaning; reading your memorial only adds grief and shame."

literal: Before long he also held Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: He soon also became grand tutor of the heir apparent.

literal: When the Taiji Hall was to be built, the emperor received the ministers at Taihua Hall and said: "We follow our predecessors' intent and will raise palace halls; the laborers have arrived and the work will begin within days.
idiomatic: When the Taiji Hall was to be built, Gaozu received the ministers at Taihua Hall and said: "We follow our predecessors' intent and will raise palace halls; the laborers have arrived and the work will begin within days.

literal: We now wish to move to Yongle to escape dust and clamor.
idiomatic: We now wish to move to Yongle to escape dust and clamor — so the record runs.

literal: Though in timber and earth I am again without heart, can destroying them fail to wring grief!
idiomatic: Though I am no builder at heart, how can tearing them down fail to wring my heart!

literal: We therefore now face you and take leave together.
idiomatic: I have called you here to take leave together.

literal: This hall was made by Emperor Gaozong, passed through Emperor Xianzu, and in my tender years I received the throne here.
idiomatic: This hall was built by Emperor Gaozong, passed through Emperor Xianzu, and in my tender years I received the throne here.

literal: But affairs seize feeling; there will be a change in design. Looking up to days past, I am only deeply grieved."
idiomatic: But necessity overrides sentiment, and the design must change. Looking back on those days fills me only with grief."

literal: Liang bowed his head and replied: "Your subject has heard that consulting divination is recorded in the canonical classics; using it to resolve doubt is honored in ancient and modern times alike.
idiomatic: Liang bowed and replied: "Your subject has heard that consulting divination is recorded in the canonical classics; using it to resolve doubt is honored in ancient and modern times alike.

literal: The work of construction is not easy to accomplish; I pray Your Majesty consult the milfoil and tortoise to fix whether it may proceed.
idiomatic: The work of construction is not easy to accomplish; I pray Your Majesty consult the milfoil and tortoise to fix whether it may proceed — so the record runs.

literal: Moreover last year's labor projects accomplished very much—the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Bright Hall were finished within a year.
idiomatic: Moreover last year's labor had already accomplished much—the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Bright Hall were finished within a year.

literal: If works are raised year after year, I fear the people's strength will be carved to exhaustion.
idiomatic: If works are raised year after year, I fear the people will be exhausted.

literal: Moreover timber has just been freshly cut and will not stand firm as work; I wish to wait further years and give the people a little ease."
idiomatic: Moreover timber has just been freshly cut and will not stand firm as work; I wish to wait further years and give the people a little ease." — so the record runs.

literal: Gaozu said: "If in the end it is not done, it may be as you say.
idiomatic: Gaozu said: "If in the end it is not done, it may be as you say — so the record runs.

literal: But when it must later be done, what good is waiting another year?"
idiomatic: But when it must later be done, what good is waiting another year?" — so the record runs.

literal: I have looked far back at former kings—none failed to build.
idiomatic: I have looked far back at former kings, and none failed to build.

literal: Therefore when Zhou founded its enterprise it raised the Spirit Terrace;
idiomatic: When Zhou founded its enterprise it raised the Spirit Terrace;

literal: when mighty Han received the Mandate, Weiyang was made.
idiomatic: when mighty Han received the Mandate, Weiyang was built.

literal: At the very founding they were still like this; how much more I, who inherit the fortune of many sages and stand on a foundation of great peace.
idiomatic: Even at founding they did as much; how much more should I, inheriting many sages' fortune upon an age of great peace.

literal: Moreover now the eight directions are clear and calm and the year's grain has again ripened—seize this time to complete the great work.
idiomatic: Moreover the eight directions are clear and calm and the year's grain has ripened again—seize this time to complete the great work.

literal: Man's allotted portion fixes short and long life; though milfoil and tortoise may be wise, what can they do against fate?
idiomatic: A man's allotted span fixes short life or long; milfoil and tortoise may be wise, but what can they do against fate?

literal: One must entrust it to the great allotment—how could it depend on divination!"
idiomatic: What fate entrusts does not wait on divination!"

literal: Thereupon he moved his residence to Yongle Palace.
idiomatic: He moved his residence to Yongle Palace.

literal: Later, when Gaozu held court in the Hall of Audience, he told Liang: "The rites of the Three Dynasties had the sun rise for audience at court; from Han and Wei downward, ceremony gradually decayed.
idiomatic: Later at the Hall of Audience Gaozu told Liang: "The Three Dynasties held court as the sun rose; from Han and Wei onward ceremony decayed.

literal: The Jin ordinance had on the first and fifteenth of the month the gathering of ministers at the Hall of Audience to discuss government, yet there was no text of the Son of Heaven attending in person.
idiomatic: Jin ordinances gathered ministers on the first and fifteenth to discuss government, yet never required the Son of Heaven in person.

literal: Now because you gather at midday, before noon you yourselves shall discuss government; after noon I shall deliberate with you what may or may not be done."
idiomatic: Now that you gather at midday, before noon you shall discuss government among yourselves; after noon I shall deliberate with you what may or may not be done."

literal: Thereupon he ordered memorials read aloud and personally decided them.
idiomatic: He then had memorials read aloud and decided them himself.

literal: He also told Liang: "Xuzhou has memorialized granting grain rations to submitted barbarians.
idiomatic: He also told Liang: "Xuzhou has memorialized granting grain rations to submitted barbarians — so the record runs.

literal: The king is the people's parent; truly it should be granted.
idiomatic: The king is the people's parent; truly it should be granted — so the record runs.

literal: But now Jing and Yang are not submissive, the written track is not one; we mean personally to lead the six armies and ask guilt of the Jiang region.
idiomatic: But now Jing and Yang are not submissive, the written track is not one; we mean personally to lead the six armies and ask guilt of the Jiang region — so the record runs.

literal: Reckoning ten thousand households submitting, a year's grain would be a million; if we heed granting it, the border stores will be emptied.
idiomatic: Reckoning ten thousand households submitting, a year's grain would be a million; if we heed granting it, the border stores will be emptied — so the record runs.

literal: Though we gain a thousand myriad households, we still have not achieved unity.
idiomatic: Though we gain a thousand myriad households, we still have not achieved unity — so the record runs.

literal: For now we wish to follow poverty in relief—what is your view?"
idiomatic: For now we wish to follow poverty in relief—what is your view?" — so the record runs.

literal: Liang replied: "What you preserve is far-reaching; it is truly as the sacred edict says."
idiomatic: Liang replied: "What you preserve is far-reaching; it is truly as the sacred edict says." — so the record runs.

literal: When the imperial carriage moved south, he was transferred to Grand General of Martial Guards and, in his existing office, supervised central military affairs.
idiomatic: When the capital moved south he was made grand general of martial guards and, retaining his existing posts, oversaw central military affairs.

literal: When Gaozu campaigned south, he put Liang in charge of Masters of Writing affairs and left him to guard Luoyang.
idiomatic: On the southern campaign Gaozu put Liang in charge of Masters of Writing affairs and left him to guard Luoyang.

literal: Later Gaozu from Xiaoping Ford was about to take a boat to Shiji; Liang admonished: "Your subject has heard the teaching of not leaning over the hall's edge—a rule from antiquity to the present; to think of danger in security is set forth in the Book of Changes.
idiomatic: Later Gaozu was about to take a boat from Xiaoping Ford to Shiji; Liang admonished: "Your subject has heard the teaching of not leaning over the hall's edge—a rule from antiquity to the present; to think of danger in security is set forth in the Book of Changes.

literal: Therefore relying on peril without guarding ends in drowning without mourning.
idiomatic: Therefore relying on peril without guarding ends in drowning without mourning — so the record runs.

literal: Even a common man's baseness still does not lightly endanger himself; how much more the honor of ten thousand chariots, upon whom living beings rely—can it be neglected!
idiomatic: Even a common man does not lightly endanger himself; how much more the honor of ten thousand chariots, upon whom living beings rely—can it be neglected!

literal: Hence at rest one dwells in deep palace and broad hall; in motion one has ten thousand riders and a thousand chariots.
idiomatic: Hence at rest one dwells in deep palace and broad hall; in motion one has ten thousand riders and a thousand chariots — so the record runs.

literal: Of old a Han emperor wished to cross the Wei by boat; Guangde was about to stain the chariot wheels with blood from his head, and the emperor was moved and went to the bridge.
idiomatic: Of old a Han emperor wished to cross the Wei by boat; Guangde threatened to stain the chariot wheels with his own blood, and the emperor was moved to take the bridge instead.

literal: That one crossing of a small stream was still like this; how much more the great river's vast flood, with immeasurable peril!
idiomatic: That one crossing of a small stream was still so perilous; how much more this great river's vast flood, with immeasurable peril!

literal: Moreover the carriage is driven by men, and even so there is the harm of running wild to ruin; how much more the river's slow or swift current, which men do not control—if disaster comes outside all foresight, what of the ancestral temple!
idiomatic: Moreover the carriage is driven by men, and even so there is the harm of running wild to ruin; how much more the river's slow or swift current, which men do not control—if disaster comes outside all foresight, what of the ancestral temple! — so the record runs.

literal: Gaozu said: "The Minister of Works speaks rightly."
idiomatic: Gaozu said: "The minister of works is right."

literal: When Liang's elder brother Pi was implicated in Mu Tai's rebellion, Liang entrusted his office affairs to the marshal Murong Qi and submitted a memorial impeaching himself.
idiomatic: When Liang's elder brother Pi was implicated in Mu Tai's rebellion, Liang entrusted office affairs to marshal Murong Qi and memorialized to impeach himself.

literal: Gaozu issued a gracious edict and would not permit it, ordering him to resume his duties.
idiomatic: Gaozu answered graciously and would not permit it, ordering him to resume his duties.

literal: Liang repeatedly and firmly refused; only after long delay was he permitted.
idiomatic: Liang firmly refused; only after long insistence was permission granted.

literal: Before long he was made bearer of the staff of authority, General Who Campaigns North, with an open office and ceremonial insignia equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Ji Province.
idiomatic: He was soon made bearer of the staff of authority, general who campaigns north, with an open office and ceremonial insignia equal to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Ji province.

literal: His fief was changed to Duke of Dunqiu with five hundred households, to continue the ennobled line.
idiomatic: His fief was changed to duke of Dunqiu with five hundred households, to continue the ennobled line.

literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was transferred to Inspector of Ding Province; before long he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Director of the Masters of Writing, and soon after transferred to Minister of Works.
idiomatic: At Shizong's accession he was made inspector of Ding province; before long he was grand general of agile cavalry and director of the Masters of Writing, and soon after minister of works.

literal: In the third year of Jingming he died, at age fifty-two.
idiomatic: He died in Jingming year 3, at fifty-two.

literal: He was given the warm-bright secret coffin of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, four hundred thousand cash, seven hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred jin of wax.
idiomatic: He was given the warm-bright secret coffin of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, four hundred thousand cash, seven hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred jin of wax — so the record runs.

literal: Shizong personally attended the lesser obsequies.
idiomatic: Shizong personally attended the lesser obsequies — so the record runs.

literal: Posthumously he was made Grand Commandant and given charge of Sizhou; his posthumous title was Kuang.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand commandant and given charge of Sizhou; his posthumous title was Kuang.

literal: His son Shao, courtesy name Yongye.
idiomatic: His son Shao, courtesy name Yongye — so the record runs.

literal: Gaozu, because he was a noble minister's hereditary scion, showed him special regard.
idiomatic: Gaozu, seeing him a noble minister's hereditary scion, showed him special regard.

literal: At nine he was made Outer Gentleman and attended study in the Eastern Palace; he was transferred to Heir Apparent Attendant.
idiomatic: At nine he was made outer gentleman and attended study in the Eastern Palace; he was transferred to heir-apparent attendant.

literal: At eleven he married the Princess of Langye and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and Literary Tutor to Prince of Jingzhao Yu.
idiomatic: At eleven he married the princess of Langye and was made commandant of the horse guards, regular attendant of scattered cavalry, and literary tutor to Prince of Jingzhao Yu.

literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Companion to Prince of Gaoyang Yong.
idiomatic: At Shizong's accession he was regular attendant of direct communication and companion to Prince of Gaoyang Yong.

literal: When he met with his father's mourning, an edict ordered him to rise and inherit the title, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and commander of the Masters of the Imperial Wardrobe.
idiomatic: When his father died an edict ordered him to rise from mourning, inherit the title, take regular attendant of scattered cavalry, and command the masters of the imperial wardrobe.

literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Minister of the Imperial Household; he was again transferred to General of the Guards and Minister of Ceremonies.
idiomatic: He became director of the palace secretariat, attendant-in-ordinary, grand master of the golden seal and purple ribbon, and minister of the imperial household; he was again made general of the guards and minister of ceremonies.

literal: Before long he was made bearer of the staff of authority, commander of military affairs in Ji and Ying provinces, in his existing rank as general and as Inspector of Ji Province; because his mother was old he firmly declined, offended the edict, and was dismissed.
idiomatic: He was soon made bearer of the staff of authority and commander of military affairs in Ji and Ying, retaining his rank as general and inspector of Ji; pleading his mother's age he firmly declined, offended the throne, and was dismissed.

literal: He was made Director of the Secretariat, transferred to Minister of the Seven Arms, and moved to Director of the Palace Department.
idiomatic: He was made director of the secretariat, transferred to minister of the seven arms, and moved to director of the palace department.

literal: He met with mourning for his birth mother and was dismissed; in residence for mourning he was famed for filial piety.
idiomatic: When his birth mother died he left office; his mourning conduct won renown for filial piety.

literal: He was again made Grand General of the Guards, Left Grand Master of the Palace, Director of the Palace Secretariat, again Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Rectifier of his native commandery.
idiomatic: He later returned as grand general of the guards, left grand master of the palace, director of the palace secretariat, again attendant-in-ordinary, and rectifier of his native commandery.

literal: Shao had no other talent, but his nature was square and weighty; he rarely received guests and seldom crossed others' thresholds.
idiomatic: Shao had no special talent, but his nature was square and grave; he rarely received guests and seldom crossed another man's threshold.

literal: The commander Yuan Cha, when power blazed, once went to Shao's residence; Shao merely met and escorted him down the steps, and men of the time admired and exalted this.
idiomatic: When commander Yuan Cha's power blazed, he once visited Shao's house; Shao merely met him at the gate and saw him down the steps, and contemporaries admired him for it.

literal: When Empress Dowager Ling wished to depose Cha but hesitated and had not decided, Shao urged approval.
idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling wished to depose Cha but hesitated, Shao urged her to act.
